E0404

`ok`/`err` need a fallible context

What

`ok`/`err` need a fallible context

Why

The registered sema rule applies here

Fix

Follow the guidance for E0404

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E0404: tests/ui/enum_pattern_needs_dot_payload.stderr.

Error [E0367]: pattern `Fade` needs a leading `.`
  --> tests/ui/enum_pattern_needs_dot_payload.jet:8:9
    |
  8 |         Fade(n) -> { print(n) }
    |         ^^^^
 Why: match patterns take a leading dot so the name isn't read as a variable or call (D-ENUMDOT1)
 Fix: write `.Fade(…)`

Error [E2417]: explicit failure domain `String (text)` is not an Error type
  --> tests/ui/enum_pattern_needs_dot_payload.jet:6:31
    |
  6 | fn show(light: Light, result: Int !String, value: Int | String) {
    |                               ^^^^^^^^^^^
 Why: A `!` contract may name `Err`, a Core error, a type marked `#Error`, an all-error union, or `Never`; arbitrary value types do not describe failures.
 Fix: use a Core error, add `#Error` to a local error type, or remove the explicit error contract.
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E2417

Error [E0116]: `print` doesn't hand back a value
  --> tests/ui/enum_pattern_needs_dot_payload.jet:15:21
    |
 15 |         Int(n) -> { print(n) }
    |                     ^^^^^
 Why: a call is a value only when its function declares a result after the parameter list
 Fix: inside an arm, wrap the call in `{ … }`; otherwise put `print` on its own line, or declare it as `fn print(…) Type -> …`
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0116

    |                        ^^^^^
 Why: a call is a value only when its function declares a result after the parameter list
 Fix: inside an arm, wrap the call in `{ … }`; otherwise put `print` on its own line, or declare it as `fn print(…) Type -> …`

Error [E0404]: `Ok(...)` only fits where a fallible result is expected
  --> tests/ui/enum_pattern_needs_dot_payload.jet:21:25
    |
 21 |     show(Light.Fade(1), Ok(1), 2)
    |                         ^^^^
 Why: `Ok` builds the success side of a `T !E` result
 Fix: use it in a `T !E` return type, a `T !E` binding annotation, or a call that expects one
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0404
